question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this experiment-gated core Claws lifecycle and Doctor diagnostics surface now, or defer it until the Claws RFC establishes the intended core/plugin ownership boundary?
rationale: The patch is a new cross-cutting product capability rather than a repair to an established contract, and repository policy reserves owner-specific optional lifecycle behavior for extension seams unless core ownership is intentionally chosen.

options.title: Sponsor the core experiment
options.body: Accept the Claws lifecycle direction, review the stacked prerequisites as one architecture decision, and land this diagnostic slice only after its ownership dependencies are approved.

options.title: Pause for RFC direction
options.body: Keep this PR open but defer merge until maintainers resolve whether the lifecycle manager and its diagnostics should live in core or an extension boundary.

options.title: Redirect to an extension design
options.body: Ask for a plugin or ClawHub-oriented implementation if the required lifecycle behavior can use existing public seams without new core ownership policy.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC direction
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but defer merge until maintainers resolve whether the lifecycle manager and its diagnostics should live in core or an extension boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct involvement in this maintainer-labeled experimental stack; no stronger decision-owner signal is available in the supplied history.
